nodes.text: Welcome to the Amberford bank. Deposits at the counter, withdrawals at the counter, and the vault behind me holds both, which is the entire cleverness of the institution.

choices.text: Why does a ford town have a bank?

nodes.text: Use the *bank chests* — one by each rug. What you put in is yours, recorded twice and touchable from any bank chest in any town, because coin in a ledger travels faster than coin in a pocket and is considerably harder to stab. The service is free. Solvency is its own advertisement.

My father kept the ford toll in a wooden box with a wooden lock. The autumn the Redmasks chained the ford and walked off with it, the town learnt what I'd been saying for years: _wood remembers nothing._ Stone and ink remember everything. Captain Aldis broke the chain; I built the vault. Between us it hasn't happened twice.

Bursar Odele, Bank of Silverfall. Every charter bank on the two roads clears through her vault row. Her letters arrive with each caravan — terse to the point of geology. I have kept every one. In this business, a dry correspondent is worth a wet mine.
The ledger notes your visit. It notes everything. Good day.
